key: series:1/series_description
    // Please describe the experimental series - what is done, with what aim, and where its record comes from (leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: written by Claude Code from the notes of the series and the stock solutions (Laura Fadler, Meng Kong, 2026-10-05/06/07)
Synthesis of Prussian blue analogues (PBA) by co-precipitation in the K1 Start annular flow reactor of Lab 208 (Accelerated Materials). Solution A (potassium ferrocyanide) and solution B (nickel(II) chloride, in experiment 2 mixed with manganese(II) nitrate) are poured from stock solutions made up beforehand into two 500 mL bottles and pumped into the coaxial capillaries of the reactor, with compressed air as the core gas; the PBA precipitates from the ions in the mixing zone and is collected as a suspension in a beaker. Experiment 1: nickel; experiment 2: nickel and manganese. Planned by Meng Kong, performed by Chuyue Li.

    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Contact_Zone has several phases - which of them cross at its ends (its ports)? Each gets its own PortCrossing transfers. [LiquidPhase "Contact_Zone_Liquid_Phase", GasPhase "Contact_Zone_Gas_Phase"] (several separated by ';')

key: series:1/task:for-Concentration_Manganese2PlusIon_Phase_Manganese_Pour_Phase_Reference_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Please describe Assuming the manganese(II) concentration (required: what is assumed, and why it may be assumed)?
    // source: C: Meng Kong, 2026-10-14 - 'The concentration of the Manganese should be at the same concentration as that of Nickle for 1:1 ratio - but not record so put it as an assumption.'
The concentration of the manganese(II) nitrate solution is not recorded. It is taken as that of the nickel(II) chloride solution, 0.01 M, for the 1:1 ratio of the two metals - and so 0.005 M in bottle no. 2 of experiment 2, where the two solutions were mixed 1:1 by volume.

key: series:1/task:for-Flowrate_Material_Stream_Air_MFC_Evidence_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Please describe Logging the run (optional, leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: the run logs K1-Li-Data/0410 (Laura Fadler, 2026-10-07)
The K1 control software logs the run every 2.4 s - air mass flow rate and air temperature at the mass flow controller, the pump set points and pressures; it saves the log when the run stops; the log of experiment 2 holds both of its runs, one after the other. The pressure of pump B reads 0.0 throughout - perhaps only its baseline, why is not known (Meng Kong, 2026-10-08) - and is not taken.

key: series:1/task:Filling_the_feed_bottles/description
    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Please describe Filling the feed bottles (optional, leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: Chuyue Li, given by Laura Fadler and Meng Kong, 2026-10-07, C2
The first task of each experiment - the ferrocyanide stock solution poured into bottle no. 1, the nickel(II) chloride stock solution into bottle no. 2; in experiment 2 the manganese(II) nitrate stock solution as well, mixed with the nickel one in bottle no. 2 - the two in equal volumes, just enough for one run (Meng Kong, 2026-10-14). It takes around 10 to 20 minutes (Meng Kong, 2026-10-08).

key: series:1/task:Running_the_K1_reactor/description
    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Please describe Running the K1 reactor (optional, leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: written by Claude Code (2026-10-07) from the draft sheet; decisions by Laura Fadler and Meng Kong as cited - assumed by Claude Code where marked ASSUMPTION
The two solutions are pumped into the reactor with the air core; the PBA precipitates in the mixing zone and the suspension runs into the beaker.

key: series:1/task:Priming_the_K1_system/description
    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Please describe Priming the K1 system (optional, leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: Laura Fadler, 2026-10-07, D1, N6

key: series:1/task:Rinsing_the_K1_system/description
    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Please describe Rinsing the K1 system (optional, leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: Laura Fadler, 2026-10-07, D1, D3, N7
After the run, like priming, with water (after experiment 1) or dilute sulfuric acid (after experiment 2, the last of the day); repeated while the pressure stays higher than normal - one rinse each, as long as priming - three minutes (Meng Kong, 2026-10-08).

key: series:1/experiment:2/task:for-Transfer_Chloride_ion-PortCrossing-from-Outlet_Liquid_Phase-to-Sample_Draw_Liquid_Phase_k1_reactor_001_outlet_tip_outlet_Occurrence_Reference_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:ExperimentSpecific] Please describe Assuming the procedure around the run (required: what is assumed, and why it may be assumed)?
    // source: C: written by Claude Code (2026-10-07) from the draft sheet; decisions by Laura Fadler and Meng Kong as cited - assumed by Claude Code where marked ASSUMPTION
Only the reaction run is logged. That the system was primed with water from beaker no. 2 before the run, rinsed after it (with water after experiment 1, with dilute sulfuric acid after experiment 2), that everything leaving the outlet tip was collected in beaker no. 1, which was emptied after experiment 2 (Meng Kong, 08.10.2026), and that one sample was taken in a falcon tube per experiment, is assumed as Chuyue Li describes the procedure.

key: series:1/experiment:1/task:for-Task_Experimental_procedure_StartTime_Reference_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:ExperimentSpecific] Please describe Assuming the times of the experiments (required: what is assumed, and why it may be assumed)?
    // source: C: written by Claude Code (2026-10-07) from the draft sheet; decisions by Laura Fadler and Meng Kong as cited - assumed by Claude Code where marked ASSUMPTION
Only the runs themselves are logged. Filling the feed bottles takes 10 to 20 minutes, priming and rinsing three minutes each (Meng Kong, 08.10.2026). Experiment 1 is taken to start 23 minutes before its run (14:02:25) - filling at most 20 minutes, then priming - and at the latest 13 minutes before it (filling at least 10 minutes). The first run of experiment 2 is not dated (it ended before the second began, 15:06:21); experiment 2 is taken to start right after experiment 1, whose run ended at 14:27:25 and whose rinse took three minutes (14:30:25). No end of the experiments is assumed. The tasks between are placed no earlier than the start of their experiment, priming at the latest three minutes before the (first) run, rinsing and emptying no earlier than the end of the (last) run.

key: series:1/experiment:2/task:for-Task_Emptying_the_waste_beaker_StartTime_Reference_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:ExperimentSpecific] Please describe Assuming the times of the experiments (required: what is assumed, and why it may be assumed)?
    // source: C: written by Claude Code (2026-10-07) from the draft sheet; decisions by Laura Fadler and Meng Kong as cited - assumed by Claude Code where marked ASSUMPTION
Only the runs themselves are logged. Filling the feed bottles takes 10 to 20 minutes, priming and rinsing three minutes each (Meng Kong, 08.10.2026). Experiment 1 is taken to start 23 minutes before its run (14:02:25) - filling at most 20 minutes, then priming - and at the latest 13 minutes before it (filling at least 10 minutes). The first run of experiment 2 is not dated (it ended before the second began, 15:06:21); experiment 2 is taken to start right after experiment 1, whose run ended at 14:27:25 and whose rinse took three minutes (14:30:25). No end of the experiments is assumed. The tasks between are placed no earlier than the start of their experiment, priming at the latest three minutes before the (first) run, rinsing and emptying no earlier than the end of the (last) run.
